questions.question: Which Asian country ranked as the happiest in the World Happiness Report 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Taiwan**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• **Taiwan** emerged as the happiest country in Asia in the **World Happiness Report 2025**, which evaluates global happiness levels based on various criteria such as **social support, life expectancy, freedom, and corruption levels**. 

• The **World Happiness Report** is a landmark survey published annually by the **United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network**. It ranks countries based on surveys and data from sources like the **Gallup World Poll**. 

• **Taiwan's high ranking** is attributed to its strong social infrastructure, high-quality healthcare system, effective governance, and emphasis on community support. 

• In recent years, Taiwan has focused on improving **mental health awareness**, environmental sustainability, and quality of life, contributing significantly to its happiness ranking. 

• Countries are rated on parameters such as **GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, generosity, and perceptions of corruption**, where Taiwan excelled among its Asian counterparts. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **World Happiness Report:** 
 

• The **World Happiness Report** is an annual publication that ranks countries based on their levels of happiness, using data from surveys conducted by organizations such as the **Gallup World Poll**. 

• Key indicators include **economic performance**, social support, life expectancy, freedom, generosity, and perceptions of corruption. 

• This report serves as a **benchmark** for governments and organizations to measure and improve societal well-being. 
 
 

• **Taiwan's Key Characteristics:** 
 

• Taiwan has a highly developed healthcare system that ensures **universal health coverage** for its citizens, contributing to high life expectancy and overall happiness. 

• The country emphasizes **community engagement**, environmental sustainability, and mental health programs, which align with the metrics of happiness. 

• Taiwan's citizens benefit from **strong economic stability**, with high GDP per capita and robust government initiatives to promote well-being. 
 
 

• **Comparison with Other Asian Countries:** 
 

• **Singapore:** Known for its high economic stability and healthcare standards, but lower rankings in social freedom and perceptions of corruption impacted its happiness score. 

• **Japan:** Despite its advanced economy and healthcare, lower social engagement and perceptions of isolation affected its ranking. 

• **South Korea:** Faced challenges like high-pressure lifestyles and mental health issues, which contributed to relatively lower happiness scores. 
 
 

• **Global Context:** 
 

• Globally, countries like **Finland**, **Denmark**, and **Switzerland** frequently top the happiness rankings due to their strong focus on social support, governance, and quality of life. 

• The **World Happiness Report** serves as an important tool for analyzing the correlation between governance, economic policies, and societal well-being. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Happiness Metrics:** 
 

• The **Gallup World Poll** collects data on various happiness indicators, which include social freedom, perceptions of corruption, and economic stability. 

• Countries are ranked based on a score derived from these metrics, making comparisons across regions possible. 
 
 

• **Significance of the Report:** 
 

• The **World Happiness Report** is used by policymakers globally to understand areas for improvement in societal well-being. 

• It offers insights into the connection between **economic policies, governance, and societal happiness**.

questions.question:
The Doppler effect describes the change in observed frequency of a wave when there is relative motion between the source of the wave and the observer.

Which of the following scenarios illustrates the Doppler effect for sound?

options.text: Light from a distant star appears shifted towards the red end of the spectrum.
A stationary observer hears a change in the pitch of a siren as an ambulance passes by.
Water waves bend as they move from deep to shallow water.
Sunlight is dispersed into different colors when it passes through a prism.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A stationary observer hears a change in the pitch of a siren as an ambulance passes by.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Doppler Effect:** It is the change in the observed frequency or wavelength of a wave due to the relative motion between the source of the wave and the observer. This phenomenon applies to sound, light, and other types of waves.
 
• **Sound Waves:** In the given scenario, the pitch (frequency) of the ambulance siren appears higher as it approaches the stationary observer and lower as it moves away. This is due to the compression and stretching of sound waves caused by relative motion. This is the correct example of the Doppler effect.
 
• **Relative Motion:** The Doppler effect specifically occurs when there is relative motion between the wave source (ambulance siren) and the observer (stationary person). The frequency changes based on whether the source is moving toward or away from the observer.
 
• **Applications:** The Doppler effect for sound waves is widely used in applications like radar speed detection, medical ultrasound imaging, and astronomy to measure the velocity of moving objects.
 
• **Incorrect Options:** Other scenarios mentioned, like light shifts and wave bending, do not describe the Doppler effect for sound waves. They pertain to different physical phenomena like refraction or dispersion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Redshift and Blueshift:** The Doppler effect also applies to light waves. When a light source moves away from the observer, its wavelength stretches, causing a redshift. Conversely, when it moves closer, the wavelength compresses, causing a blueshift. This is used in astronomy to study the movement of stars and galaxies.
 
• **Refraction:** The bending of waves, such as water waves moving from deep to shallow water, is due to a change in wave speed and direction. This phenomenon is not related to the Doppler effect.
 
• **Dispersion:** Sunlight splitting into different colors when passing through a prism is due to dispersion. Different wavelengths of light refract at slightly different angles, creating a spectrum. This is unrelated to the Doppler effect.
 
• **Applications of Doppler Effect:** In sound waves, it is used in technologies like Doppler radar, which measures the speed of objects such as vehicles. In medical settings, Doppler ultrasound is used to monitor blood flow and heart conditions.
 
• **Important Formula:** The change in observed frequency due to the Doppler effect for sound waves can be calculated using: f′=fv+vov+vs" id="MathJax-Element-1-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">f′=fv+vov+vsf′=fv+vov+vs f′=fv+vov+vs f' = f \frac{v + v_o}{v + v_s} , where: - f' : Observed frequency - f : Actual frequency - v : Speed of sound - v_o : Speed of observer - v_s : Speed of source

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1:** Light from a star shifted toward the red spectrum is an example of the Doppler effect for light waves, not sound waves.
 
• **Option 3:** Water waves bending due to a change in medium is refraction. It doesn’t involve frequency change due to motion.
 
• **Option 4:** Dispersion of sunlight into colors is caused by differences in refractive index, unrelated to the Doppler effect.
 
• **Real-Life Example:** The siren of an emergency vehicle passing by is the most common and relatable example of the Doppler effect for sound waves.
 
• **Discovery:** The Doppler effect was first described by Austrian physicist **Christian Doppler** in **1842**.

questions.question: Find the INCORRECT statement about Gram staining of bacteria.

options.text: Gram positive bacteria have a thick peptidoglycan layer so they are unable to retain crystal violet
Gram negative bacteria have thin layer of peptidoglycan and cannot retain the crystal violet
Grams iodine is responsible for the formation of the crystal-violet-iodine complex
Gram-negative bacteria appear red/pink under a microscope

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Gram positive bacteria have a thick peptidoglycan layer so they are unable to retain crystal violet.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gram-positive bacteria** have a **thick peptidoglycan layer** in their cell wall, which allows them to retain the crystal violet-iodine complex during Gram staining. This is why they appear **purple** under the microscope. *The statement is incorrect.*
 
• **Gram-negative bacteria** have a **thin peptidoglycan layer** and an outer membrane, which makes them unable to retain the crystal violet dye after the decolorization step. Instead, they take up the counterstain (safranin), appearing **red/pink**. *This statement is correct.*
 
• **Gram’s iodine** acts as a mordant, forming a complex with crystal violet dye, known as the **crystal violet-iodine complex**, which is retained in Gram-positive bacteria. *This statement is correct.*
 
• After the Gram staining process, **Gram-negative bacteria** appear **red/pink** under the microscope due to the uptake of the counterstain. *This statement is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gram Staining Process:**
 
 
• The Gram staining technique was developed by **Hans Christian Gram** in **1884**.
 
• It is a differential staining method that classifies bacteria into two groups: **Gram-positive** and **Gram-negative**.
 
• The steps involve:
 
 
• Application of **crystal violet** (primary stain).
 
• Addition of **Gram’s iodine** (mordant).
 
• Decolorization with **alcohol or acetone**.
 
• Counterstaining with **safranin**.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Differences Between Gram-positive and Gram-negative Bacteria:**
 
 
• Gram-positive bacteria have a **thick peptidoglycan layer** and lack an outer membrane.
 
• Gram-negative bacteria have a **thin peptidoglycan layer** and an **outer membrane** composed of lipopolysaccharides.
 
• The outer membrane in Gram-negative bacteria acts as a barrier to certain antibiotics and dyes.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Gram Staining:**
 
 
• It is widely used in clinical microbiology to identify bacterial infections.
 
• It helps guide the selection of antibiotics by distinguishing between Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.
 
• It is also used in research to study bacterial morphology and structure.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Gram-positive and Gram-negative Bacteria:**
 
 
• **Gram-positive:** *Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae*, *Bacillus subtilis*.
 
• **Gram-negative:** *Escherichia coli, Salmonella typhi, Pseudomonas aeruginosa*.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Why Gram Staining is Important:**
 
 
• It provides a quick and preliminary identification of bacteria in clinical samples.
 
• It differentiates bacteria based on their cell wall structure, which is critical for understanding their pathogenicity and antibiotic susceptibility.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Gram Staining:**
 
 
• Some bacteria, such as **Mycobacterium** (e.g., *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*), do not stain well with Gram staining due to their waxy cell walls and require special staining techniques like **acid-fast staining**.
 
• Gram staining is not effective for identifying viruses as they lack a cell wall.

questions.question: Which of the following is a new offense defined under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Terrorist act**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023** is a significant reform in Indian criminal law, aimed at replacing the British-era Indian Penal Code (IPC) 1860 with more modern and relevant provisions. 
 
• One of the new offenses defined under this law is a **Terrorist act**, which addresses acts of terrorism that threaten India's sovereignty, unity, integrity, and security. 
 
• The definition of a **Terrorist act** under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, includes provisions that cover acts of violence, disruption of public order, and damage to critical infrastructure, intending to create fear or coerce the government. 
 
• This reform expands the legal framework to combat terrorism more effectively, ensuring stricter penalties and enhanced investigation mechanisms for terrorist activities. 
 
• Other offenses like **criminal intimidation, adultery, and sedition** were already covered under the repealed IPC, but terrorism has been elaborated upon as a distinct and critical offense in the updated legislation. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:** 
 
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill, 2023**, was introduced in Parliament as part of a broader effort to modernize India’s criminal justice system. 
 
• This law aims to replace the **Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860**, which was drafted during British colonial rule. 
 
• It incorporates provisions for **modern crimes** such as cybercrime, terrorism, and organized crime. 
 
• The bill emphasizes the principles of justice and equality, ensuring that the laws are in sync with the **21st-century challenges**. 
 
 
 
• **Key features of the Terrorist Act under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023:** 
 
 
• Defines terrorism comprehensively, including acts causing **terror, fear, or coercion**. 
 
• Addresses activities that disrupt **sovereignty, integrity, and public order** in India. 
 
• Includes provisions for **stringent punishments**, such as life imprisonment and death penalties for severe offenses. 
 
• Provisions for **seizure of properties** and financial assets linked to terrorism. 
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Sedition:** 
 
 
• The offense of **sedition** under Section 124A of the IPC has been **repealed** in the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. 
 
• However, provisions dealing with acts threatening **sovereignty and integrity** have been incorporated under the new law. 
 
• This reflects a shift in focus from suppressing dissent to addressing **real and tangible threats** to national security. 
 
 
 
• **Criminal Intimidation and Adultery:** 
 
 
• **Criminal Intimidation** continues to be a punishable offense under the new law, but it is not a newly defined offense. 
 
• **Adultery** was decriminalized by the **Supreme Court of India in 2018** through its verdict in the **Joseph Shine case**. 
 
 
 
• **Modern Challenges Addressed:** 
 
 
• The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, aims to strengthen the legal framework against crimes such as **terrorism, cybercrime, and organized crime**. 
 
• It aligns India's criminal justice system with global standards, ensuring **timely justice** for victims and effective deterrence for offenders.

questions.question: Which dance from Gujarat is performed with sticks during Navratri?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dandiya Raas**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• **Dandiya Raas** is a traditional folk dance originating from the state of **Gujarat**, India, and is performed during the **Navratri festival**. 

• The dance is characterized by the use of **decorated wooden sticks**, known as **Dandiyas**, which participants strike together rhythmically to the beat of the music. 

• **Dandiya Raas** represents the dramatization of the battle between the goddess **Durga** and the demon **Mahishasura**, symbolizing the victory of good over evil. 

• It is a group dance, traditionally performed in a circular formation, with dancers energetically moving in sync with the music, often accompanied by vibrant traditional attire. 

• This dance form is widely popular not only in Gujarat but across India, particularly during the **9-day Navratri celebrations**, making it a significant cultural tradition. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Garba:** 
 

• Another popular dance form from **Gujarat**, performed during **Navratri**. 

• Unlike Dandiya Raas, Garba involves circular movements performed without sticks and emphasizes graceful hand and foot movements. 

• Garba is performed in honor of **Goddess Durga**, and participants usually dance around a centrally placed **light or deity**. 
 
 

• **Kolattam:** 
 

• Kolattam is a traditional stick dance from the state of **Tamil Nadu**. 

• It is performed in groups with synchronized stick movements, and while it shares similarities with Dandiya Raas, it is culturally distinct. 

• Kolattam is often associated with temple festivals and is performed to devotional songs. 
 
 

• **Perini Shivatandavam:** 
 

• Perini Shivatandavam is a historic dance form from **Telangana**, dedicated to **Lord Shiva**. 

• This dance is considered a warrior dance, traditionally performed to invoke the spirit of Shiva before going to war. 

• Unlike Dandiya Raas, it does not involve sticks but focuses on vigorous movements and expressions. 
 
 

• **Navratri Festival:** 
 

• Navratri is a **9-day Hindu festival** celebrated across India, dedicated to the worship of the **Goddess Durga**. 

• It is marked by fasting, prayers, and cultural events, including folk dances like **Dandiya Raas** and **Garba**. 

• Navratri celebrations differ across regions, showcasing the diversity of India’s cultural heritage. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Significance of Dandiya Raas:** 
 

• The sticks used in Dandiya Raas symbolize the **sword of Goddess Durga**. 

• The dance promotes **community bonding** as it is performed in groups, often fostering joy and unity among participants. 

• The music accompanying Dandiya Raas is typically traditional folk songs, often sung in **Gujarati**, adding authenticity to the cultural experience. 
 
 

• **Modern Adaptations:** 
 

• While traditionally performed in villages, Dandiya Raas has gained popularity in urban areas and is now organized in large-scale events. 

• Modern Dandiya events often include **fusion music**, combining traditional beats with contemporary tunes to attract younger participants. 

• The attire has evolved to include vibrant and stylish costumes inspired by Gujarati tradition, enhancing the visual appeal of the dance.

1. Hooghly region
2. Kolhapur-South Kannada region
3. Gujarat region
4. Vishakhapatnam-Guntur region
5. Durg-Raipur region
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hooghly Region:** This is a major industrial area in India, primarily located in West Bengal. It includes industries like jute, textiles, engineering, and chemicals along the Hooghly River. *Hence, this is a major industrial region.*
 
• **Kolhapur-South Kannada Region:** This region is not considered a major industrial area compared to other regions in India. While it has industries, its scale and contribution to India's industrial output are relatively limited. *Hence, this is NOT a major industrial region.*
 
• **Gujarat Region:** Gujarat is one of India's most prominent industrial hubs, with major industries like petrochemicals, textiles, pharmaceuticals, and diamond cutting. *Hence, this is a major industrial region.*
 
• **Vishakhapatnam-Guntur Region:** Located in Andhra Pradesh, this region is a significant industrial center with industries like steel, shipbuilding, fertilizers, and chemicals. *Hence, this is a major industrial region.*
 
• **Durg-Raipur Region:** Situated in Chhattisgarh, this region is known for its steel and iron industries and is a key industrial area in central India. *Hence, this is a major industrial region.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hooghly Industrial Region:**
 
 
• Located in **West Bengal**, this region is known for jute manufacturing, textiles, and engineering industries.
 
• It benefits from proximity to Kolkata, easy access to ports, and abundant labor.
 
• Major industries include **jute mills, paper mills, chemicals, and engineering products.**
 
 
 
• **Gujarat Industrial Region:**
 
 
• Gujarat is one of the fastest-growing industrial regions in India, with cities like Ahmedabad, Surat, and Vadodara leading the way.
 
• Key industries include **petrochemicals, pharmaceuticals, textiles, and diamond processing.**
 
• The state is well-known for its SEZs (Special Economic Zones) and ports.
 
 
 
• **Vishakhapatnam-Guntur Region:**
 
 
• This region is an important industrial hub in Andhra Pradesh, with major industries including steel plants, shipbuilding, and chemical production.
 
• Vishakhapatnam is home to India's **largest shipyard** and significant defense industries.
 
• It also has significant contributions to agriculture-based industries like fertilizers.
 
 
 
• **Durg-Raipur Industrial Region:**
 
 
• This region in Chhattisgarh is primarily known for its steel and iron industries.
 
• It houses the Bhilai Steel Plant, one of India's largest steel manufacturers.
 
• Other industries include **cement, aluminum, and power generation.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Industrial Regions in India:**
 
 
• Industrial regions are formed due to factors like resource availability, transportation facilities, skilled labor, and proximity to markets.
 
• India's industrial regions are concentrated in states like **Maharashtra, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Karnataka.**
 
• Examples of major regions include Mumbai-Pune, Ahmedabad-Vadodara, Chennai-Coimbatore, and Delhi-Faridabad.
 
 
 
• **Role of Industrial Regions:**
 
 
• Industrial regions contribute significantly to India's GDP and employment.
 
• They act as hubs for innovation, technology, and manufacturing.
 
• These regions often facilitate international trade due to their proximity to ports and airports.
 
 
 
• **Kolhapur-South Kannada Region:**
 
 
• While this region has industries, it is not as prominent or developed as other major industrial hubs in India.
 
• Industries in this region are smaller in scale and focus on local and regional markets.

questions.question: In case of a conflict between Central and State law on a Concurrent List subject, the State law prevails only if:

options.text: It is passed by a two-thirds majority
It is supported by a Supreme Court ruling

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It has received Presidential assent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In India, the **Concurrent List** refers to subjects on which both the **Central and State governments** can legislate, as per the **Seventh Schedule of the Constitution**.
 
• When there is a conflict between a **Central law** and a **State law** on a matter in the Concurrent List, the **Central law generally prevails** under **Article 254(1)** of the Constitution.
 
• However, if a **State law** that is inconsistent with a **Central law** has been passed and subsequently **receives Presidential assent**, it will prevail in that particular state under **Article 254(2)**. This is an exception to the general rule.
 
• The Presidential assent allows the State law to override the Central law, but the overriding effect is limited to the territory of that specific state.
 
• This provision reflects the federal nature of India's governance, allowing states some flexibility in dealing with matters where there may be unique regional requirements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concurrent List under the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• The **Concurrent List** is one of the three lists under the **Seventh Schedule** of the Constitution, alongside the Union List and the State List.
 
• Subjects in the Concurrent List include matters such as **education, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy, forests, and criminal law**, where both the Center and States can legislate.
 
• This list allows for **cooperative federalism**, ensuring both levels of government can address issues of national and regional importance.
 
 
 
• **Presidential Assent:**
 
 
• **Presidential assent** is the approval given by the President of India for a bill passed by a state legislature that conflicts with an existing Central law.
 
• Under **Article 254(2)**, once a state bill receives Presidential assent, it can prevail within that specific state even if it is inconsistent with the Central law.
 
• This mechanism ensures a balance between the **autonomy of states** and the overarching authority of the Central government.
 
 
 
• **Article 254 of the Constitution:**
 
 
• **Article 254(1):** If there is a conflict between laws made by the Center and the State on a Concurrent List subject, the Central law will prevail.
 
• **Article 254(2):** A State law that conflicts with a Central law can prevail in the state if it receives Presidential assent, but this does not affect the validity of the Central law in other parts of the country.
 
• This provision highlights India's **quasi-federal structure**, where states have limited autonomy in legislative matters.
 
 
 
• **Examples of State Override:**
 
 
• One notable example is the **Maharashtra Animal Preservation Act**, which received Presidential assent and prevails over Central laws related to animal preservation in Maharashtra.
 
• Such instances underscore the importance of Presidential assent in addressing **regional legislative priorities**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the President:**

 
 
• The President's role in granting assent is crucial as it ensures the **constitutional validity** of laws enacted by state legislatures that may conflict with Central laws.
 
• By granting assent, the President upholds the principles of **federalism** while ensuring the legislative needs of individual states are met.
 
 
 
• **Union vs State Legislation:**

• Conflicts are resolved through mechanisms like **Presidential assent** or judicial review.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Interpretation:**
 
 
• The judiciary plays a significant role in interpreting **Article 254** and resolving disputes related to legislative conflicts.
 
• Several landmark cases have clarified the scope and application of state laws that override Central laws with Presidential assent.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Kho-Kho rules is correct?

options.text: A chaser may change direction only within free zones outside the poles.

The chasing team has all nine players sitting in the central lane during attack.
Early kho is when the active chaser taps the runner after calling 'kho'.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 
 
• **A chaser may change direction only within free zones outside the poles:** This is a correct statement. In Kho-Kho, the chaser is allowed to change direction in the free zone near the poles, which ensures smooth gameplay and prevents obstruction in the central lane. This rule maintains the integrity of the game and allows the chasers to strategize effectively. 
 
• **A runner is not out even if they step outside the playing area while escaping:** This statement is incorrect. In Kho-Kho, runners stepping outside the designated playing area are considered out as they are violating the boundaries of the game. The rule ensures fair play and prevents runners from gaining an unfair advantage. 
 
• **The chasing team has all nine players sitting in the central lane during attack:** This statement is incorrect. While the chasing team has players sitting in the central lane, not all nine players are actively chasing at the same time. Only one active chaser pursues the runners, while the others wait for their turn. 
 
• **Early kho is when the active chaser taps the runner after calling 'kho':** This statement is incorrect. An early 'kho' refers to a scenario where the active chaser gives a ‘kho’ prematurely, violating the rules of the game. Tapping the runner after calling 'kho' signifies a legitimate chase and does not relate to an early kho. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__

• Kho-Kho is a traditional Indian sport that emphasizes speed, agility, and teamwork. 
 
• The game is played by two teams, each consisting of 12 players, but only 9 players are allowed to play actively during an innings. 
 
• It originated in Maharashtra, India, and has gained international recognition through tournaments and events. 
 
 
 
• **Free Zones:** 
 
 
• The free zones are areas near the poles where chasers can change direction. 
 
• These zones are crucial for tactical gameplay and ensure smooth transitions for the chasing team. 
 
 
 
• **Basic Rules of Kho-Kho:** 
 
 
• The game is divided into two innings, with each team taking turns as chasers and runners. 
 
• The primary objective of the chasing team is to tag all runners within the given time frame. 
 
• Runners aim to avoid being tagged by the chasers while staying within the designated playing area. 
 
 
 
• **International Recognition:** 
 
 
• Kho-Kho is governed by the Kho-Kho Federation of India (KKFI) and has expanded its reach globally. 
 
• The sport has been included in events such as the Asian Games and South Asian Games, showcasing its popularity. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• Chasers must utilize the free zones effectively to change directions and strategize their chase. 
 
• Communication among chasers is vital to ensure a coordinated effort in tagging runners. 
 
 
 
• **Runner's Techniques:** 
 
 
• Runners must maintain agility and avoid predictable movements to evade chasers. 
 
• Staying within the boundaries is essential to avoid being declared out.

• The referee ensures adherence to rules and resolves disputes during the game.

questions.solution:

__ 
 
• **Statement 1: Short Line Measurements**: 
 
 
• In a **singles squash court**, the short line is marked at a distance of **4.26 m from the back wall.** 
 
• In a **doubles squash court**, the short line is positioned at **4.57 m from the back wall.** 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
 

 
• **Statement 2: Tin Height**: 
 
 
• The **tin** is a **48 cm high strip** located at the front wall of a squash court. 
 
• Its purpose is similar to that of a tennis net, acting as a lower boundary for valid shots. 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
 

 
• **Statement 3: Half-Court Line and Short Line Forming an L**: 
 
 
• The **half-court line** and the **short line** intersect at the center of the court to divide it into four quadrants. 
 
• However, this does not form an "L" with the back wall as a base; instead, it forms a “T” shape at the center. 
 
• This statement is **incorrect**.

• The **singles squash court** measures 9.75 m (length) by 6.4 m (width). 
 
• The **doubles squash court** is larger, measuring 13.72 m (length) by 7.62 m (width). 
 
• The height of the court walls varies but must meet international standards set by the World Squash Federation (WSF). 
 
 

 
• **Purpose of the Tin:** 
 
 
• The tin prevents players from hitting the ball too low on the front wall. Any ball that strikes the tin is considered out. 
 
• In professional squash, it adds a level of precision and difficulty for players.
 
 

 
• **Markings on the Squash Court:** 
 
 
• The **short line** divides the court into front and back halves. 
 
• The **half-court line** divides the back half into two equal parts, creating left and right service boxes. 
 
• The **service boxes** are used to initiate play during serves. 
 
 

 
• **Rules of Squash:** 
 
 
• The objective is to strike the ball onto the front wall within the boundaries, ensuring it doesn’t hit the tin or go out of bounds. 
 
• The ball must bounce only once on the floor before being returned by the opponent.
 
• Matches are typically played in a best-of-5 games format, with each game requiring a player to score 11 points to win. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• It ensures uniformity across professional tournaments and oversees the development of the sport globally.
 
 

 
• **Squash Ball Specifications:** 
 
 
• Squash balls are made of rubber and vary in bounce levels, indicated by colored dots (e.g., double yellow for professionals).

• Eye protection is mandatory in many tournaments to prevent injuries from the fast-moving ball.

questions.question: **Read the statements given below carefully :****Statement 1:** The Deccan Trap region of the Peninsular Plateau is covered with black soil derived from igneous rocks.**Statement 2:** The Aravalli Hills are newly formed folded mountains stretching from Gujarat to Delhi.**Which of the above statements is/are correct?**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• **Statement 1:** The Deccan Trap region of the Peninsular Plateau is covered with **black soil** derived from **igneous rocks.** 
 
 
• The Deccan Trap is a large volcanic province in west-central India formed by extensive volcanic eruptions during the **Cretaceous period.** 
 
• The rocks in this region, primarily basalt, weather over time to form **fertile black soil**, also known as **regur soil.** 
 
• The black soil is highly suitable for growing crops like **cotton**, hence it is also called **black cotton soil.** 
 
• *Hence, this statement is correct.* 
 
 

 
• **Statement 2:** The Aravalli Hills are newly formed folded mountains stretching from Gujarat to Delhi. 
 
 
• The Aravalli Hills are among the **oldest mountain ranges** in the world, dating back to the **Precambrian era** (approximately 3.2 billion years ago). 
 
• They are not newly formed; rather, they are highly eroded and weathered over time due to their geological age. 
 
• The range extends from **Rajasthan** and **Haryana** through parts of **Gujarat** to **Delhi.** 
 
• *Hence, this statement is incorrect.* 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Black Soil Characteristics:** 
 
 
• Black soil is rich in **calcium carbonate, magnesium, potash, and lime**, making it highly fertile. 
 
• It has a high water retention capacity, which is beneficial for crops like **cotton, sugarcane, wheat, and oilseeds.** 
 
• This soil develops cracks during the dry season, which helps in better aeration. 
 
 

 
• **Formation of Deccan Trap:** 
 
 
• The Deccan Traps were formed by **successive volcanic eruptions** that occurred about **65 million years ago**. 
 
• The eruptions resulted in the creation of a massive layer of **igneous rocks** that later weathered to form black soil. 
 
 

 
• **Aravalli Hills Features:** 
 
 
• The Aravallis are composed of **ancient crystalline rocks**, such as granite, quartzite, and gneiss. 
 
• They are considered **relic mountains**, significantly eroded over millions of years. 
 
• The range is a critical source of **minerals**, including lead, zinc, and marble, and plays an important role in environmental conservation. 
 
 

 
• **Importance of Aravalli Range:** 
 
 
• The Aravalli Hills act as a natural barrier against the spread of the **Thar Desert** into the eastern parts of India. 
 
• They are home to a variety of **flora and fauna** and serve as a crucial ecological zone in the region. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• The Deccan Plateau covers a large part of southern India and is known for its **volcanic origin**. 
 
• The Aravallis have a significant role in influencing the **climate** of the region by blocking hot desert winds. 
 
• Black soil is found predominantly in the **Deccan Plateau** states such as Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Madhya Pradesh. 
 
• The Aravalli range has faced severe ecological degradation due to **deforestation, mining, and urbanization.**

Consider the following statements regarding India's Green Credit Programme:
1. It provides credits for verified voluntary environmental actions like afforestation and water harvesting.
2. It operates under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
3. Credits are tradable and recognized by financial institutions.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All 1, 2, and 3 are correct**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
__ 

• **India's Green Credit Programme** is designed to incentivize individuals, institutions, and industries to undertake **voluntary environmental actions** such as afforestation, water harvesting, waste management, and energy efficiency measures. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.* 

• The programme operates under the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**, which is a key legislation for environmental protection in India. It provides the legal framework for the programme's implementation. *Hence, statement 2 is correct.* 

• Credits earned through the programme are **tradable**, meaning they can be bought and sold in the market. These credits are recognized by **financial institutions**, enabling participants to monetize their environmental efforts. *Hence, statement 3 is correct.* 

• The Green Credit Programme represents a significant step towards **sustainable development** by aligning economic incentives with environmental conservation. 

• **Tradable credits** allow industries and businesses to offset their environmental footprints by investing in green initiatives. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
__ 

• **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986:** 

• This act was enacted in **1986** following the Bhopal gas tragedy to provide measures for the protection and improvement of the environment. 

• It empowers the central government to take all necessary measures to protect the environment and prevent pollution. 

• The act is comprehensive, covering aspects such as emissions, hazardous waste management, and environmental standards. 
 
 

• **Green Credit Trading Mechanism:** 

• Trading allows entities that perform better environmentally to sell their **credits** to those that fall short, thus encouraging widespread adoption of green practices. 

• Examples include **carbon credits**, which are similar in concept but focus specifically on reducing greenhouse gas emissions. 
 
 

• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** 

• The Green Credit Programme aligns with several SDGs, including **SDG 13 (Climate Action)** and **SDG 15 (Life on Land)**, by promoting afforestation and reducing environmental degradation. 

• It also indirectly supports **SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth)** by creating economic opportunities through green initiatives. 
 
 

• **Global Examples of Green Credit Systems:** 

• Countries like **China** have implemented similar programmes, such as the **China Certified Emissions Reduction (CCER)** system. 

• The European Union operates the **Emissions Trading System (EU ETS)**, which is one of the largest carbon trading platforms globally. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 

• **Afforestation:** 

• Afforestation involves planting trees in areas that were not previously forested, helping mitigate climate change by sequestering **carbon dioxide**. 

• India's Green Credit Programme promotes afforestation as a key activity for earning credits. 
 
 

• **Water Harvesting:** 

• Water harvesting techniques help conserve water resources, reduce dependence on groundwater, and ensure sustainable water management. 

• Such initiatives are crucial for addressing water scarcity in drought-prone regions. 
 
 

• **Waste Management:** 

• Efficient waste management practices, such as recycling and composting, reduce landfill waste and promote a circular economy. 

• India's Green Credit Programme encourages industries to adopt sustainable waste management systems. 
 
 

• **Energy Efficiency:** 

• Improving energy efficiency reduces energy consumption and emissions, contributing to sustainable industrial growth. 

• Participants in the Green Credit Programme can earn credits by implementing energy-efficient technologies and practices. 
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Why was the rupee devalued in 1991?

options.text: To boost exports and attract foreign exchange

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To boost exports and attract foreign exchange**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 
 

• The **1991 economic crisis** in India was marked by a severe balance of payments deficit, high inflation, and dwindling foreign exchange reserves. The reserves had fallen to less than **$1 billion**, barely enough to cover two weeks of imports. 

• The Government of India decided to devalue the **Indian Rupee** on **July 1 and July 3, 1991**, by around **18-19%** against foreign currencies to address the crisis and stabilize the economy. 

• Devaluation was aimed at making **Indian exports more competitive** in the global market by reducing their prices in terms of foreign currencies, thereby increasing demand for Indian goods. 

• The move was intended to attract **foreign exchange inflows** by boosting exports and encouraging remittances from the Indian diaspora, which would help improve foreign reserves.

Regarding solar system planets:
1. All Jovian planets have solid surfaces.
2. Uranus's axis of rotation is nearly parallel to its orbit.
Which of the above is are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

 
 
• **Statement 1:** "All Jovian planets have solid surfaces." 
 
 
• This statement is **incorrect**. Jovian planets, also known as gas giants, include Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. They are primarily composed of hydrogen, helium, and other gases and lack a solid surface. Instead, they have thick atmospheres and possibly small, dense cores deep inside.
 
• These planets are characterized by their massive sizes, rings, and numerous moons but do not have surfaces like terrestrial planets (e.g., Earth or Mars).
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** "Uranus's axis of rotation is nearly parallel to its orbit."
 
 
• This statement is **correct**. Uranus is unique among the solar system planets due to its extreme axial tilt of approximately 98 degre

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:**
1. Schedule VI applies to tribal areas in Assam and Tripura.

2. Autonomous Councils under Schedule VI can make laws on forest management.

3. Schedule VI is applicable to Jharkhand.

Which of the above is/are correct**?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1: 1 and 2 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Schedule VI** of the Constitution of India is applicable to the **tribal areas** in states like **Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram**. It provides for the administration of tribal areas through Autonomous District Councils (ADCs). ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Under Schedule VI, the Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) are empowered to make laws on several subjects, including **forest management**, land use, water resources, agriculture, and village administration. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Jharkhand** is not covered under Schedule VI of the Constitution. The tribal areas in Jharkhand are governed by other provisions such as the Fifth Schedule.
